privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.e2e: Messages are not end-to-end encrypted. Server administrators can read messages through the database.

privacy.intro: This policy explains what data natter collects, how it is used, and how long it is kept. natter is a small, independently run messaging project, so we aim to keep this short and plain.

p: If you sign in with Google, we receive your Google account identifier, email address and name. We use the name only as your initial display name.
When you set up your profile, we store the username and display name you choose.
When you chat, we store the messages you send, the conversations you are part of, and which messages have been read.
If you continue as a guest, we create a temporary account without any personal information.
Your data is used only to run the service: signing you in, letting other people find you by username, and delivering your messages. We do not sell your data, show ads, or share it with third parties.

Messages are not end-to-end encrypted. They are stored on our server, and server administrators can read them through the database. Please do not share passwords, financial details or other sensitive information on natter.
Conversations are deleted after 1 month of inactivity.

A guest session ends 30 minutes after the last message, or when the guest logs out or ends the session. The account is then deactivated and can no longer be used. A guest who sent no message is deleted immediately.

The conversation of a deactivated guest, including any contact information the guest voluntarily shared, is kept on the developer's side for up to 1 month after the last message, then deleted automatically.
Sharing contact information as a guest is voluntary.
We use cookies only to sign you in and keep you signed in. Your theme and language preferences are stored in your browser. We do not use tracking or analytics cookies.
You can change your display name in Settings, and you can delete your account at any time. Deleting your account removes your profile, conversations and messages.

When you continue as a guest, we use Cloudflare Turnstile to check that you are not a bot. Turnstile processes data from your browser, such as your IP address and browser characteristics, to make this decision. This data is handled by Cloudflare under its own privacy policy and is not stored by natter.
If we change this policy, we will update the date at the top of this page.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: By using natter you agree to these terms. They are short on purpose.

p: natter is a personal project provided as is, without any guarantee of availability, reliability or that data will be kept. It may change or stop at any time.
Do not use natter for spam, harassment, or any illegal content.
The developer may delete accounts that break these rules, without notice.

sections.h: 3. Messages are not private from the server
p: Messages are not end-to-end encrypted. Server administrators can read them through the database. Do not share passwords or other sensitive information.

When a guest session ends (30 minutes after the last message, logout or End session), the account is deactivated. Its conversation, including any contact info the guest shared, is kept for the developer for up to 1 month after the last message, then deleted. Guests who sent no message are deleted immediately.
Conversations are deleted after 1 month without activity.
You can delete your own account at any time from Settings.
natter is limited to 300 accounts. When the limit is reached, new sign-ups are paused until space is available.
These terms may change. When they do, we will update the date at the top of this page. Continuing to use natter means you accept the updated terms.
